messages:
lisa: FYI customer T-942 escalated — their audit-export bucket shows missing shards for 2026-03-15 and the forwarder pods returned 403s right after last-night's KMS rekey. attaching logs below. :alarm_clock:

omar: quick snippet from forwarder logs (rotated keys at 23:14 UTC):
```
2026-03-15T23:14:07Z forwarder-0 ERROR encrypt: AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform kms:Encrypt on key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/old-key-id
2026-03-15T23:14:08Z forwarder-0 WARN push: zero-byte manifest created for shard tenant=T-942 shard=2026-03-15-23
```

security-bot: Alert: KMS alias "alias/audit-export" was updated by infra@redwood 2026-03-15T23:12:45Z. Linked resources: forwarder-deployment-prod.

kevin: @eng-infra-jay can you confirm if the forwarder was pinned to a key ID instead of alias? If so that would explain the 403s after alias swap. :thinking_face:

eng-infra-jay: we deployed rekey to rotate master key id -> new-key-id but a few clusters still referenced the raw key id in env var (KMS_KEY_ID). can repro on staging. repro steps below.

eng-infra-jay: repro (staging):
```
# simulate forwarder pod using old key id
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/forwarder KMS_KEY_ID=111:old-key-id
kubectl rollout restart deploy/forwarder
kubectl logs deploy/forwarder -c forwarder | grep Encrypt
```

omar: also saw the S3 manifest list for tenant T-942 show empty shards for that hour; listing returns zero objects even though events were ingested server-side. suspect encrypt failure caused forwarder to skip commit.

sara-support: Customer says their SIEM didn't receive events between 23:12 and 23:30. They're asking for exact event ids to reconcile. We promised a timeline to the customer. :clock3:

lisa: mitigation ideas? short-term: add a KMS grant to allow old principal -> encrypt with new key alias? long-term: make forwarder use alias not raw key id.

kevin: short-term plan I suggest:
- add grant for forwarder role to new-key-id with Encrypt/Decrypt
- restart forwarder canary and verify no 403s
- replay the skipped shard(s) from primary event store to export path
Acceptance criteria: manifests present in S3 for 2026-03-15 23:00-23:30 and SIEM acked them.

eng-infra-jay: I can add the grant and restart canary now. running quick check in staging first.

omar: repro curl to check manifest present (customer-facing snippet):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <support-token>" https://storage.redwood.example/exports/T-942/manifests/2026-03-15/23
# returns 403 or an empty JSON array
```

lisa: runbook notes: if forwarder returns encrypt AccessDenied we treat shard as failed and emit a zero-byte manifest to keep sequence. that caused the gap. we should add clearer telemetry that flags "encrypt-failure" metric.

eng-infra-jay: can confirm grant applied to prod forwarder role, restarting canary (pod/forwarder-7b8). will watch logs.

omar: after restart, staging logs show encrypt succeeded with alias and objects written to S3:
```
2026-03-15T23:22:01Z forwarder-7b8 INFO encrypt: success key=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:alias/audit-export
2026-03-15T23:22:02Z forwarder-7b8 INFO push: manifest uploaded tenant=T-942 shard=2026-03-15-23 size=14.2KB
```

lisa: ok owners and next steps:
- eng-infra-jay: confirm prod grant + restart all forwarder pods (ETA 30m) :fire_engine:
- omar: run replay job for tenant T-942 for window 23:10-23:40 and verify S3 manifests (I will kick off and monitor).
- sara-support: update customer with ETA and offer partial export of available events now.

kevin: one follow-up: schedule a config audit to find any other deployments hardcoding KMS_KEY_ID. create a short PR to prefer KMS_ALIAS over key id.

lisa: thanks team. will update thread with replay job id and customer note when available. :thumbsup:
